records.localization_note: Use approved Rafael Castor. Verify the same protagonist's given name and surname in the installed dialogue substitutions.
Use approved Maria Li in the dialogue header. The catalogue's Huamei corresponds to the separate source field.
Keep Janus Pasar. His hesitant question about Linares does not establish a title for Janus or Linares.
Keep Claudio Manaus in the header and the established Clau nickname where Rafael speaks it.
Keep Julio Erneco. His warning in the quarrel uses only the approved personal name in the header.
Keep Arcadius Eudoxios in the public header. Rafael uses Eirene in private and the catalogue preserves the source middle field.
Keep Xien Yan. His respectful transition to Admiral Li does not create a rank for him.
Use Pedro Valdes in the dialogue and Pedro de Valdes in the catalogue, consistent with the source's separate middle particle.
Keep the established Barbarossa Hayreddin in the header and the source's separate Fazul in the catalogue.
Keep Simon Linares. The separate given name and surname match Valdes's address and Simon's claim about his Cordoban family.
Shopkeeper suits the merchant who reports the fleet movements in town. Leave the source's background descriptor out of the speaking label.
Trader identifies the trading-house worker who asks about the fight off Seville and warns Rafael.
Trader also identifies the separate informant who points Rafael to Hangzhou. His casual voice and regional knowledge come from his dialogue.
Port Worker fits the dock attendant who welcomes Rafael and relays the summons. The familiar Japanese form grants no office or kinship.
Priest preserves the role that matters when he offers the object upon Rafael's Mediterranean victory.
Guildmaster identifies the guild leader whose advice is to stay clear until the fleet is ready.
Sailor suits the affiliated crew member cheering aboard. Keep the broader Retainer form for the catalogue.
